Tongue dry, cracked; blood like ink exudes,

odor.

Spinal irritation, tingling of lower extremi-

Cold, dry hands and feet of excessive

Shriveled, numb ; mottled dusky-blue tinge.

Coldness; cold, dry skin; cold, clammy
sweat; excessive thirst. Sense of internal heat.

Worse, heat, warm covering. Better,
cold, uncovering, rubbing, stretching out limbs.

Objective. Exhalations from the.skin, of a vinous odor (fifth
day), 155 .—Exhalations from the skin fetid (second day), 155 .—Desquamation
of the whole body three times, in a girl, 47 .—[940.] The epidermis begins

— Dry and withered appearance of skin, 116 .—The skin, which in general
was inclined to perspiration, was constantly quite dry, 124 .—Dryness of the
skin, with no trace of perspiration, 139 .— *Skin dry and cool , 135 .—The capil¬
lary action of the skin was remarkably slow, a portion of the skin deprived
of its blood, by pressure with the finger, being a long time in recovering

—[950.] Skin hot, dry, and of a yellowish-brown color, resembling that of
a mulatto (second and third days); hot, dry, but not as dark as it was the
day before (fourth day) ; hot and dry, but of a better color, of a natural
appearance on the feet and hands (sixth day) ; soft and more natural to
the touch, but still very yellow (ninth day) ; yellow, soft, and moist (tenth


573

day); moist and yellow (eleventh day), 155 .—Skin dry and of a muddy-
yellow hue.(second and third days), 156 *—Skin discolored, 142 —Skin had a

she can be cut and pricked without pain, or without blood flowing from

gangrenous and died altogether; the gangrene rapidly extended over

the neck, 34 .—A painless blister on the left index finger, as large as a nut,

over the whole body,* 2 .—* Formication in the tips of the fingers, lasting several

tween the skin and flesh, 1 * 0 .—Jerking crawling under the skin , 31 .— 11 Sensation

stitches, here and there, in the skin, disappearing on scratching, soon re¬

ness (sixth, eighth, and ninth days), 155 .—Strong desire to sleep (after one

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Chilliness. Extremely violent chill, followed by burning
heat, especially affecting internal parts, and associated with violent anxiety,
so that many lose their reason, with violent, almost unquenchable thirst, 61 .
— Violent chill, followed by violent burning heat, with unquenchable
thirst, 6 *.—A chill came on, followed immediately by nausea, sharp pain in
the head, with dizziness and partial blindness, 156 .—Rigors, with cutis anse-
rina, 125 .—Rigors, followed by heat and violent thirst (first day), 155 .—Shaking
chill, 48 .—Creeping chill over the extremities (after one hour); chilliness
over the whole body (after three hours), 126 .—[1030.] General sensation of
coldness in different parts of the body, as from cold water or from snow, 89 .
—Sensation of cold (after one hour), 126 ®.—* Coldness of the surface of the
body, and particularly the extremities , 161 .—* Diminished temperature of the
body, 1 * 1 . —* Cold skin, 122 ; (after three-quarters of an hour), 106 .—* Skin cold,
